why: Commits 2 and 3 describe two new measuring tools in prose and leave real choices in code the brief has not shown. For render-modes: what counts as a hole's 'matching completion', which file serves '/', and what the house store's route is ('read its slug from CI's seed step'). For server-budget: how to insert 500 products with prices by generate_series 'copying the required columns' when prices may only change through commerce.set_price, and a time-window filter for background statements. Both become hard gates in CI's e2e job, so a flaky or wrong design turns CI red for every push.
harm_if_wrong: A server-budget or render-modes script that is unstable or measures the wrong thing would fail CI's e2e job at random, blocking every push that carries a migration (they wait for all checks), or would hold numbers that do not mean what the docs say.
make_it_cheaper: Give budget-seed.mjs's SQL in full (including how the price is set: through commerce.set_price), give the house store's slug and the exact hole-completion rule ('B:n' matched by a '<div hidden id="S:n"' in the same file), and give the commits a statement-count reading to start from; then commits 2 and 3 become cheap-then-review.
brief_problems: The count command it gives (rg -c "['\"]use cache" src -g '!*.test.*') prints 91 today, not 85: comments and strings also match. Only a match of whole directive lines gives 85, so the model may think the scan is wrong.
budget-seed.mjs is told to insert prices directly by insert … select, but CLAUDE.md says prices only change through commerce.set_price; a trigger may refuse it, or the model may bypass the rule.
Depends on step 1.9's src/db/statement-count.ts and the client.query wrapper, neither of which exists today; commit 3 cannot start before it.
The new CI steps pipe to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY but exit 1 on a regression, so they are hard gates, not just summaries; the brief does not say so, nor how flakiness is handled beyond one retry.
